sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Afghanistan
sources.organization: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) and Norwegian Institute of International Affairs (NUPI)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate observations through 2024; displacement and socioeconomic conditions through 2025; selected projections to 2039-2050
sources.methodology: SIPRI/NUPI fact sheet synthesizes climate, conflict and security evidence.
sources.limitations: Secondary synthesis; climate rarely drives conflict.

sources.title: Favorable harvest temporarily improves food access despite lingering drought impacts
sources.temporal_coverage: July 2026-January 2027 food security outlook; 2026 harvest and late-July flooding
sources.methodology: FEWS NET update summarizes current food insecurity and geographic projections.
sources.limitations: High-level outlook page; projected food security outcomes are not a climate attribution analysis and are limited to the stated forecast period.

sources.title: Two in three Afghan households show resilience gains in last year
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.temporal_coverage: Household resilience assessment results for 2023-2024; interventions since 2021
sources.methodology: FAO publisher summary reports E-RIMA resilience changes among supported households.
sources.limitations: Summary omits sampling and comparison details; findings are not nationally representative.

claims.paraphrase: Central, northern and northwestern provinces face agricultural drought amid low coping capacity and high ecological and socioeconomic fragility.
claims.limitations: Broad regional groupings; no provincial estimates.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: SIPRI links drought risk to low coping capacity and fragility (p. 2).

claims.paraphrase: Conflict-driven deforestation increases flash-flood exposure and asset loss in eastern, northern and western Afghanistan.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: SIPRI links conflict deforestation to flood exposure and loss (p. 2).

claims.locator: PDF p. 1, summary of climate-related peace and security risks
claims.paraphrase: Climate-related resource pressure can intensify water and land disputes; Taliban involvement complicates farmer-herder conflicts.
claims.limitations: Climate is not the sole conflict cause.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: SIPRI notes this resource-conflict pathway and Taliban role (PDF p. 1).

claims.locator: PDF p. 3, Migration and mobility subsection
claims.paraphrase: SIPRI reports 675,500 climate-related cross-border migrants in Apr-Dec 2025, notably from drought-affected Faryab, Ghor, Badghis and Balkh.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: SIPRI attributes movements to climate hazards (p. 3).

claims.locator: PDF p. 3, Migration and mobility subsection
claims.paraphrase: Climate displacement is a last resort; weak physical, financial and social capital and limited government support constrain adaptation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: SIPRI cites lost options, low capital and weak support (PDF p. 3).

claims.paraphrase: FEWS NET expects consecutive drought years and below-average production to keep food and income access constrained in Daykundi, Faryab, Ghor, Nimroz, Badakhshan and Kunar, despite a near-average 2026 harvest elsewhere.
claims.scenario: FEWS NET July 2026-January 2027 outlook; no climate scenario specified.
claims.limitations: Forecast is limited to the stated July 2026-January 2027 period and is not a climate-model projection.

claims.paraphrase: FEWS NET reports late-July 2026 flooding damaged homes, infrastructure, cropland and standing crops in localized parts of Nangarhar, Paktika and Kabul; it expects household losses but no area-level food-security classification change.
claims.limitations: FEWS NET characterizes the event as localized and explicitly does not project area-level deterioration from it.

claims.paraphrase: FAO reports that two-thirds of Afghan households supported by its interventions increased measured resilience capacity by at least 10% between 2023 and 2024; reported gains differed across provinces.
claims.limitations: The result is limited to intervention-supported households; the publisher summary does not provide enough detail to assess representativeness or attribution.

access_audit.notes: Opened and read the four-page fact sheet, including the migration and security-pathway passages.
Opened the publisher report page and read the July 2026-January 2027 outlook text.
FAO publisher page exposes the policy brief summary and E-RIMA results; linked full brief returned a cache-miss error and was not treated as inspected.
DOI landing fetch failed with cache miss; no claims were drawn from content beyond the official FAO summary page.
PDF fetch failed because the document exceeded the browser content-size limit; an indexed excerpt was not used.
Opened the short UN country-team summary; its concise claims were not needed in the final evidence set.

search_audit.query: Afghanistan climate drought subnational vulnerability Faryab Ghor Badghis Balkh local livelihoods 2026 source
search_audit.outcome: Opened SIPRI's updated fact sheet and FEWS NET's 2026 outlook; verified named provincial vulnerability and crop/food-access details.

search_audit.query: Afghanistan climate hazard explicit conflict mediator water land disputes farmer herder 2026 report
search_audit.outcome: SIPRI explicitly describes climate-related resource pressure and water/land disputes, complicated by Taliban involvement in farmer-herder conflict; it cautions climate is rarely the main conflict driver.

search_audit.query: Afghanistan conflict insecurity effect climate resilience adaptation water infrastructure capacity 2026 source
search_audit.outcome: SIPRI explicitly links conflict-driven deforestation to flood exposure and describes conflict/political instability as weakening resilience; no separate subnational estimate was located.

search_audit.query: Afghanistan local climate resilience capacity early warning agricultural livelihoods UN 2025 2026 report
search_audit.outcome: FAO's E-RIMA summary reports intervention-associated household resilience gains and provincial variation; the underlying full policy brief could not be fetched.

gaps: Subnational climate-conflict pathways remain unevenly documented; the SIPRI synthesis supports several explicit mechanisms but does not isolate climate's contribution to conflict outcomes.
The full FAO policy brief was inaccessible through its DOI link; its publisher summary supports only the reported E-RIMA results and methodology.
The 2026 UN Results Report PDF could not be inspected because of its size, so it was excluded.
Current provincial-level evidence on adaptation barriers for women, people with disabilities and other groups was not expanded in this pass.
